Abstract
               
                  Motivation
                  Vastly greater quantities of microbial genome data are being generated where environmental samples mix together the DNA from many different species. Here, we present Opal for metagenomic binning, the task of identifying the origin species of DNA sequencing reads. We introduce ‘low-density’ locality sensitive hashing to bioinformatics, with the addition of Gallager codes for even coverage, enabling quick and accurate metagenomic binning.
               
               
                  Results
                  On public benchmarks, Opal halves the error on precision/recall (F1-score) as compared with both alignment-based and alignment-free methods for species classification. We demonstrate even more marked improvement at higher taxonomic levels, allowing for the discovery of novel lineages. Furthermore, the innovation of low-density, even-coverage hashing should itself prove an essential methodological advance as it enables the application of machine learning to other bioinformatic challenges.
               
               
                  Availability and implementation
                  Full source code and datasets are available at http://opal.csail.mit.edu and https://github.com/yunwilliamyu/opal.
               
               
                  Supplementary information
                  Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

Abstract

Motivation
Microbial genome datasets are expanding rapidly as environmental samples increasingly contain mixed DNA from many species. We present Opal for metagenomic binning, which identifies the source species of DNA sequencing reads. By bringing low-density locality-sensitive hashing into bioinformatics and incorporating Gallager codes for even coverage, we enable fast, accurate metagenomic binning.


Results
On public benchmarks, Opal reduces precision/recall error (F1-score) by half relative to both alignment-based and alignment-free species classification methods. We also show an even larger gain at higher taxonomic levels, enabling the discovery of novel lineages. In addition, low-density, even-coverage hashing is itself an important methodological advance because it makes machine learning applicable to other bioinformatics problems.


Availability and implementation
The full source code and datasets are available at http://opal.csail.mit.edu and https://github.com/yunwilliamyu/opal.


Supplementary information
Supplementary data are available online at Bioinformatics.
